verdict.headline: Washington and Tehran near Hormuz deal that would unlock trapped Persian Gulf oil supply
verdict.label: ES +0.39% PM (SPX record 7,736 close); NQ flat (AMD −8.7% PM, SPCX −8% PM drag); WTI $75.40 (−5.7%, clearing $79 trigger); 10Y 4.619% (−7bps); Sept hike ~42% Poly; ADP 8:15 AM ET; NFP Friday
verdict.rationale_short: The dominant macro regime trade is resolving in one session: WTI crashed to $75.40 as the US-Iran Hormuz 60-day interim deal nears a Wednesday announcement, clearing both oil-side regime breaches and dropping September hike odds to ~42%. That leaves 30Y at ~5.20% as the sole remaining breach — 1-of-6 — against a record SPX close of 7,736. AMD and SPCX both sold off 8%+ AH on earnings beats-with-catches: AMD gross margin 54% vs 56% consensus (Helios AI ramp costs); SPCX $18.37B capex (6x YoY) with no Starlink profitability confirmation. These are stock-specific, not systemic AI failures — Nasdaq futures are flat rather than down, confirming the distinction. ADP at 8:15 AM ET is the intraday trigger: a soft print pushes September hike toward sub-30% and 10Y toward 4.5%, which could compress the last breach. A formal Hormuz signing today would print 1-of-6 on the regime scorecard — the most constructive reading since before the Iran escalation began.

trade_setups.asset: Hormuz deal close — energy vs. consumer re-rate
trade_setups.thesis: WTI at $75.40 has already priced significant Hormuz progress, but a formal 60-day interim signing (targeted today) unlocks the next leg toward $68–70 as trapped Persian Gulf supply restores progressively. The beneficiaries are airlines (fuel cost deflation), consumer discretionary (disposable income tailwind), and trucking/logistics — not energy producers. XOM, CVX face structural headwinds until OPEC+ cuts respond. The deal is a tradable event, not a permanent supply unlock; ceasefire risk resets at each 60-day extension.
trade_setups.entry: Formal signing = next WTI leg toward $68–70. Airlines and consumer discretionary are the vehicles. Fade energy on any rip above $78 until deal is signed and first tanker transits confirmed.
trade_setups.invalidation: Deal collapses (IRGC military action or Trump escalation) → WTI retraces to $82+ in one session; oil-side regime breaches immediately return; regime flips back to 2-of-6.
trade_setups.horizon: Resolves at Wednesday announcement; secondary check at first tanker transit confirmation

trade_setups.thesis: AMD's Q2 data-center $6.7B (+107% YoY) and Q3 guide of $13B midpoint confirms AI hardware spend is intact and AMD is capturing share. The gross margin miss (54% vs 56%) is attributed to Helios ramp costs — MI450 deployments front-loading capital. If margin recovers toward 56%+ in Q3, $440–445 is a textbook earnings-wash entry. If Helios competitive pricing has permanently moved the margin floor lower, the multiple compression is structural. Conference call Q&A on Q3 margin trajectory is the deciding data point.
trade_setups.entry: $440–445 support zone holds → next reference at $510–520. Break below $435 with volume invalidates the washout-entry thesis.
trade_setups.invalidation: Q3 gross margin guidance below 55% in the call → $420 prior support. NVDA or custom-silicon displacement commentary → structural re-rate below $400.
trade_setups.horizon: 2–4 weeks; Q3 margin clarity is the resolution

trade_setups.asset: ADP + NFP sequence — last regime breach clearing event
trade_setups.thesis: September hike at ~42% Polymarket (down from 82% on July 31) is being driven entirely by oil deflation, not labor softening. JOLTS June 7.36M was a mild miss but not a labor market collapse. ADP today and NFP Friday (consensus ~91K) are the real test. A soft ADP (< 80K) pushes September hike toward sub-30%, and a sub-75K NFP could compress the 10Y toward 4.5% and the 30Y below 5.00% — which would represent a full regime clear for the first time since the Iran escalation began. That is the most consequential data sequence remaining this week.
trade_setups.entry: Watch CME FedWatch September probability within 30 minutes of ADP (8:15 AM ET) and NFP (8:30 AM ET Friday). ADP < 80K with September hike falling toward 35% is an early full-clear signal.
trade_setups.invalidation: ADP > 200K → September hike pushes back above 55%; 30Y extends above 5.25%; the oil-relief trade is partially offset by a rate headwind re-imposition.
trade_setups.horizon: ADP 8:15 AM ET today; NFP Friday August 7

bear_case: The Hormuz deal is the market's load-bearing assumption — and it has collapsed twice in 2026 already. Any IRGC military action or Trump escalation rhetoric restores WTI to $82+ in one session, returning both oil-side breaches simultaneously and pushing September hike back above 55%. AMD's gross margin at 54% vs 56% is not obviously a temporary ramp cost: if Helios competitive pricing has permanently moved the floor, AMD's multiple compression is structural and the AI hardware thesis bifurcates between NVDA (premium, sticky) and AMD (volume, commoditizing). SPCX's $18.37B quarterly capex — with no Starlink profitability confirmation — is the most aggressive spend rate of any public company in 2026; AI revenue at $2.56B (+247% YoY) is impressive but the payback period at this capex scale is unmeasurable. 30Y at ~5.20% remains the sole regime breach; a hot ADP print reverses the narrative that labor is softening. SPX at record 7,766 is simultaneously pricing the Iran deal, labor softening, AI earnings strength, and oil deflation — that concentration creates asymmetric downside to any single factor disappointing.
